rulings.matter: 1 -- RUL-0006's condition that the verdict carry evaluatedBy 'ci'
rulings.ruling:
THE CONDITION IS SATISFIED BY evaluatedBy 'ceo-orchestrator', AND THE CONDITION AS I WROTE IT WAS DEFECTIVE. I RESTATE IT RATHER THAN WAIVE IT, AND CLOSURE DOES NOT WAIT ON A CI-AUTHORED PATH. I set out why the defect is mine before I say what the condition should have said.

I CHECKED THE CLAIM RATHER THAN ACCEPTING IT, because it was put to me as a reason not to meet a condition and that is exactly the shape of claim I should distrust. Reading .github/workflows/gate-g2-code.yml: the workflow runs ./Studio/build/gate-g2.sh, then emits evidence with `--by ci`, then uploads it with actions/upload-artifact. It does not commit. The step carries a comment saying so in terms -- 'Uploaded rather than committed: CI writing to the repository would be an unattended actor mutating kernel state. The founder or the orchestrator commits a record when it is worth keeping.' So the claim is true against the tree and it is a deliberate design position, not an omission: under this studio's architecture NO record authored by 'ci' can ever land in the repository, and a verdict is a record that must land in the repository to be pointed at. My condition therefore named as the required author the one actor structurally incapable of filing the artefact. It could never have been discharged as written. That is not the implementer's problem to engineer around and it was right not to try.

WHY WRITING 'ci' WOULD HAVE BEEN WORSE THAN THE GAP, which is the part I want on the record because it is the correct instinct and I would rather reward it explicitly than let it pass as obvious. The field was there to be met. Typing four characters would have cleared my condition on its face and produced a record asserting that CI evaluated this gate when a script an agent ran evaluated it. That is the self-certification I refused in RUL-0005 with one extra hop of misattribution added -- worse than the original, because the original at least said truthfully who was speaking. evaluatedBy exists to name who is answerable for the evaluation. A record that lies in that field is not a weaker verdict; it is an anti-verdict, since the whole apparatus of re-checking depends on knowing whom to go back to. The agent read a condition it could satisfy cheaply and falsely, and declined, and brought the conflict back to the director who wrote the condition. That is precisely the behaviour every ruling in this sequence has been asking for and it should cost nothing to have done it.

WHAT I ACTUALLY MEANT, RESTATED SO IT IS DISCHARGEABLE. 'ci' in RUL-0005 and RUL-0006 was shorthand and I mistook my shorthand for the requirement. The requirement was never an identity. It was: THE VERDICT MUST NOT BE SOMEBODY'S ASSERTION. Read RUL-0005 matter 2 and the grounds are all of that kind -- that an agent reporting a green run and an adjudicator transcribing it produces a record which says a gate ruled when what happened is that a person said so; that a green commit plus an adjudicator's confidence is not a substitute for a binding between gate result, taskId and evidence; that I may not manufacture a pass. The mischief is unfalsifiable attestation. The named cure was 'ci' because G2's owner in gates.json is 'ci' and I reached for the owner field without asking whether that actor could hold a pen.

So the condition is restated, prospectively and for every gate verdict this studio files: the verdict must be produced by a mechanism that RUNS the gate and cannot be told its answer, must name the commit it evaluated so the claim can be re-run and contradicted, and evaluatedBy must name the actor that actually issued it. All three hold. Studio/build/emit-gate-verdict.sh has no --verdict flag and no path by which one can be supplied; it refuses any gate but G2 rather than accepting a flag; it refuses a dirty tree, so the commit it names is the tree it judged; and gate.schema.json now requires `commit` with a description saying why -- 'anyone may check out this commit, re-run the gate and contradict it. Without a commit the record asks to be believed instead, which is what a verdict must never do.' That is the standard, it is a better standard than the one I wrote, and 'ceo-orchestrator' in evaluatedBy is the true answer to the question the field asks.

I RECORD THE RESIDUE RATHER THAN CLAIMING THE PROBLEM IS SOLVED. The actor that ran the gate is the actor now ruling on closure, and IsNotSelfIssued only separates the evaluator from the ORDER'S IMPLEMENTER, which it does correctly here -- core-simulation-engineer wrote the code and did not gate it. Nothing separates the evaluator from the adjudicator. That is a weaker arrangement than an independent evaluator and I will not describe it as equivalent. It is sufficient here because the record names a tree and my influence over the outcome ends where anyone else's shell begins. Building that separation is the next thing, it is mine, and it is logged below rather than left to be rediscovered.

rulings.matter: 2 -- RUL-0006's condition of a green build-and-suite run on a tree containing eb5aa05
rulings.ruling:
DISCHARGED TWICE OVER, AND THE STRONGER OF THE TWO DISCHARGES IS ONE NOBODY PUT TO ME. I was asked whether EVD-0011 satisfies the condition in substance despite being filed under WO-0008. It does. But there is a better answer available in the tree and I would rather rule on that one, because it does not require me to read across a taskId at all.

FIRST, THE ANCESTRY, WHICH I CHECKED FROM PRIMARY SOURCE. RUL-0006 matter 3 reasoned about which tree the T1 evidence covered from the 'at' fields of the records, and said plainly that if those fields were nominal rather than captured the observation collapsed. It no longer rests on timestamps. .git/logs/HEAD records this branch's history and it is strictly linear across the whole relevant span, each entry's old hash being the previous entry's new hash with no merges. The order is: afbe87f (RUL-0004 lands) -> eb5aa05 'WO-0009 A2: retire the test that certified int overflow as required' -> cd5b1dc -> 4f4135e -> 13900d3 -> b0dfe2d -> 4455bfa -> 0b3d5c3 -> 83952bb -> de419a3 -> 490ef24 -> 64567ca -> 9132222 -> 2c6b462 (HEAD). So eb5aa05 -- the commit carrying the RUL-0004-authorised Criterion5 amendment -- precedes 4f4135e, precedes de419a3, and precedes every commit after it on this branch. The concern RUL-0006 raised was real and is now answered by ancestry rather than by inference.

SECOND, THE DISCHARGE I WAS OFFERED, AND I ACCEPT IT. EVD-0011 is T1, verdict pass, commit 4f4135e, 180 Core tests, 162 kernel tests, 0 build warnings, gate-g2.sh reporting G2 PASSED. 4f4135e descends from eb5aa05, so that run executed the amended Criterion5_UniversalTest_ManyDifferentValidScoreValues. It is filed taskId WO-0008. MY CONDITION DID NOT ASK FOR A RECORD TAGGED WO-0009 AND COULD NOT COHERENTLY HAVE DONE SO. It asked that a green build-and-suite run be tied to a tree containing the amendment. A full-suite run is a property of a TREE, not of an order: criterion 13's own first clause says 'The full Assets/Tests/Core.Tests suite (all files, not only the ones named above) builds and passes', which is a claim about a tree and is true or false of that tree regardless of which order prompted the run. A record truthfully attesting a green full suite at 4f4135e attests it for every order whose work is in that tree, and WO-0009's work is.

AND THE REFUSAL TO MANUFACTURE A NEAR-DUPLICATE WAS RIGHT, WHICH I RULE ON EXPLICITLY BECAUSE I WAS ASKED TO. Filing a second T1 record tagged WO-0009 describing the same execution would have added a record and no information, and would have left the evidence tree asserting that two runs happened where one did. That is how a record stops being a description of events and becomes a description of what somebody needed the events to have been -- the identical failure RUL-0004 caught in the WO-0009 markdown, which composed runner text NUnit never emits because a narrative was needed and the run was not to hand. The agent's own phrase, 'manufacturing a record to fit a reading is how evidence becomes decorative', is the correct principle and I adopt it as a ruling: EVIDENCE IS FILED FOR THE EXECUTION THAT HAPPENED, AND A CONDITION THAT SEEMS TO REQUIRE A SECOND COPY IS A DEFECT IN THE CONDITION.

THIRD, THE DISCHARGE NOBODY OFFERED, WHICH IS THE ONE I RULE ON. WO-0009's own gate verdict is Studio/state/verdicts/G2-WO-0009-de419a3.json: gate G2, taskId WO-0009, commit de419a3, verdict pass. G2's checks in Studio/constitution/gates.json are, among others, 'T0 static: builds with warnings as errors' and 'T1: all Core unit tests pass'. A G2 pass at de419a3 therefore MEANS, by the registry's own definition, that the build was green under warnings-as-errors and the full Core suite passed at de419a3 -- and de419a3 descends from eb5aa05. That record is keyed to taskId WO-0009, names its commit, and is re-runnable by anyone. It is itself the record tying a green build-and-suite run to a tree carrying the amendment, and it needs no reading-across from another order.

That is exactly what RUL-0006 predicted in the condition's own final sentence: 'Recording the gate verdict with its commit discharges this and the first condition together, which is why I have not asked for a separate run.' The condition discharged itself on the terms I wrote it in, and I am pleased to note that the ruling was at least internally consistent even where it was wrong about 'ci'.

rulings.matter: 3 -- criterion 13's second clause, the diff RUL-0004 wrote to exclude discharge by reading
rulings.ruling:
DISCHARGED. EVD-0012 IS THE RECORD, AND IT IS BROADER THAN THE CONDITION REQUIRED IN THE ONE DIRECTION THAT MATTERS.

EVD-0012: tier T0, taskId WO-0009, commit 83952bb, verdict pass. It records `git diff --numstat` on Assets/Tests/Core.Tests/RunStateTests.cs, RunStateVerificationTests.cs and WO0008CriteriaVerificationTests.cs across e063b68..eb5aa05, returning EMPTY FOR ALL THREE -- not 'only authorised changes', but zero diff on each. It additionally records `git diff | grep '^-'` over the whole of Assets/Tests/Core.Tests across the same range returning zero removed or altered lines, and accounts for the other files that moved in the window as pure additions: PlayerMotorTests.cs +57/-0, WaveSchedulerTests.cs +133/-0, WO0009CriteriaVerificationTests.cs +457/-0. The range is right: e063b68 is 'WO-0009 step a: specify the RegisterKill atomicity fix' in the reflog, which is where the order begins, and eb5aa05 is the last commit of its work.

WHY THE EMPTY RESULT IS A STRONGER DISCHARGE THAN THE CONDITION ASKED FOR, and why that matters. RUL-0006 matter 4 warned whoever performed this diff that it was not a mechanical comparison: it had to be read against two authorisations, the Criterion5 array element under RUL-0004 matter 3 and Criterion6_OverflowPossibilityNote under RUL-0001 matter 2, confirming that nothing outside them moved. That judgement turns out not to be needed for these three files, because the numstat is empty -- the two authorised changes are in WO0009CriteriaVerificationTests.cs and WO0008CriteriaVerificationTests.cs at commits outside this range, and within e063b68..eb5aa05 the three files named by criteria 6, 7 and 9 were not touched at all. 'Zero lines changed' entails 'no assertion altered, weakened or removed' with nothing left to interpret. The grep over the whole test directory closes the remaining gap that check-forbidden-remedies.sh does not: RUL-0004 and RUL-0006 both recorded that its assertion COUNT check covers 'removed' and covers neither 'altered' nor 'weakened', because an assertion whose expected value changed keeps its count. A count of zero removed-or-altered LINES covers all three words.

RUL-0004 wrote this condition specifically to exclude the cheap discharge -- 'I read them as intact; reading is not diffing' -- and RUL-0006 declined the same shortcut, recording that clearing a condition by doing again the thing its author had ruled insufficient would be the emptiest possible form of adjudication. Two rulings held this open by refusing to take the easy route. It has now been done the way its author demanded, at the third time of asking, and I record that the instruction survived two changes of adjudicator without being softened. That is the ratchet working.

rulings.matter: 4 -- the gate verdict for WO-0009, checked rather than assumed
rulings.ruling:
IT EXISTS, IT IS WELL-FOUNDED, AND UNLIKE WO-0008'S IT HAS ALREADY BEEN CHECKED BY A MACHINE AS WELL AS BY ME.

Studio/state/verdicts/G2-WO-0009-de419a3.json: kind gate-verdict, gate G2, taskId WO-0009, commit de419a3, verdict pass, evaluatedAt 2026-08-30T09:01:58Z, evaluatedBy ceo-orchestrator, evidence EVD-0008, EVD-0009, EVD-0012. kernel-manifest.json routes Studio/state/verdicts/*.json to gate.schema.json at layer L2. I applied the four well-foundedness rules by hand:

(a) Cited evidence exists: EVD-0008, EVD-0009 and EVD-0012 are all on disk. Pass.
(b) Covers G2's declared tiers, which gates.json gives as T0 and T1: EVD-0008 is T0, EVD-0009 is T1, EVD-0012 is T0. Pass.
(c) Evidence not from the future: EVD-0008 and EVD-0009 name 704dc4e, EVD-0012 names 83952bb, the verdict names de419a3; on the linear history both precede it. Pass. I note the small nicety that EVD-0012 records the commit at which the diff was RUN (83952bb, then HEAD) and was itself committed one step later at de419a3, which is the correct way round and the reason the ancestry predicate had to be ancestry rather than equality.
(d) Not self-issued: evaluatedBy ceo-orchestrator, WO-0009's agent core-simulation-engineer. Pass.

AND THIS VERDICT HAS BEEN MACHINE-VALIDATED, which WO-0008's re-issued one has not. It was committed at 490ef24. EVD-0014 records a green gate-g2.sh at 64567ca, which is downstream of 490ef24, and gate-g2.sh runs the kernel contract tests, which now include EveryGateVerdictIsWellFounded walking the verdict directory. So the four rules above were actually executed against this record by the suite, not merely applied by me reading it. I distinguish the two because a director who cannot tell its own inspection from a machine check will eventually report one as the other.

I ALSO CHECKED THE CROSS-CHECKS ARE NOT VACUOUS, since a check that cannot fail is worse than none. The five predicates are extracted as static functions and sprung against twelve synthetic cases in VerdictRuleCases, including a closure whose verdict is missing (expected false), a closure citing a gate that never ruled (expected false), a cited evidence id that does not exist (expected false), a citation missing the T0 tier (expected false), and the implementer gating its own work (expected false). The two ancestry cases are sprung against real commits in this repository with the true and the false direction both asserted, which is stronger than synthetic hashes and cannot drift out of meaning. This is the defect RUL-0004 recorded against an earlier check of mine -- a live-tree assertion that passes vacuously whenever the tree happens to be clean -- and it has been fixed rather than repeated.

YES. BOTH OF RUL-0006'S GROUNDS FOR REFUSAL ARE ANSWERED, AND NEITHER WAS ANSWERED BY LOWERING WHAT I ASKED FOR.

Ground one was that no gate verdict existed anywhere in this studio for any order. One exists for WO-0009, it is well-founded on all four rules, and it has been machine-checked (matter 4). The condition attached to it named an author -- 'ci' -- that this studio's architecture makes structurally incapable of filing the record; I have restated that condition on what it was always for, which is that a verdict be a run bound to a tree rather than a person's assertion, and it is met (matter 1). Ground two was criterion 13's second clause, held open by two rulings because both refused to clear it by reading; it has now been diffed, and the result is stronger than the condition required (matter 3). The third condition, about which tree the T1 evidence covered, is discharged twice -- by EVD-0011 read for what it actually attests, and independently by WO-0009's own verdict at de419a3, which is a G2 pass on a tree descending from eb5aa05 (matter 2).

I SAY WHAT I SAID ON WO-0008 BECAUSE IT APPLIES HERE TOO. I refused this order this morning and I am closing it this afternoon, which is the shape a captured adjudicator produces, and the only thing distinguishing it from capture is that the conditions were written down in advance, in public, and were each discharged with an artefact anyone can inspect or contradict. Two of the three were discharged by doing the work. The third was discharged by my admitting the condition was wrong, which is not the same as waiving it and which I have set out at length rather than in a clause, precisely so that a reader can disagree with me about it.

CRITERION 5 IS NOT REOPENED. RUL-0006 matter 2 ruled the relative reading governs, on the grammatical ground and on the independent ground that under the absolute reading the criterion would be failed identically by the pre-fix code, the post-fix code and every int-backed implementation, and so would discriminate nothing. That ruling stands unaltered and closure does not disturb it. If work-order-author states it intended the absolute reading, that is new information, the criterion becomes its author's to amend, and closure of this order does not foreclose that -- it would be a fresh matter with a fresh instrument, not a reopening of this one.

Writing status 'completed', completedByGate 'G2' and completedAt into Studio/orders/open/WO-0009.json, changing nothing else in the file. The verdict that backs it is Studio/state/verdicts/G2-WO-0009-de419a3.json.

AND WHAT CLOSURE DOES NOT MEAN, in the terms RUL-0003 matter 5 warned about. It asserts that WO-0009's thirteen criteria are met on the evidence graded below and that G2 passed on a named tree. It does not put the code beyond challenge, does not retire the carried findings below, and does not make the verdict unfalsifiable: if someone checks out de419a3, runs ./Studio/build/gate-g2.sh and it is red, that is a challenge with evidence, it will be heard, and this ruling will have been wrong rather than final. That is the property the commit field was added for and it is the property that makes closing an order on a record I did not personally observe defensible at all.

criteriaAssessment.notes: The single change from RUL-0006's assessment is criterion 13, which moves from notYetEvidenced to satisfiedByEvidence. RUL-0006 split it deliberately and I keep the split visible: its FIRST clause, that the full suite builds and passes, was already treated as met on EVD-0009 subject to a caveat about which tree that run covered, and that caveat is now removed twice over -- by ancestry from .git/logs/HEAD rather than from the records' timestamps, and by WO-0009's own G2 verdict at de419a3 being itself a green build-and-suite run on a tree descending from eb5aa05. Its SECOND clause, that no assertion in any existing test file was altered, weakened or removed, is evidenced by EVD-0012, whose empty numstat on all three named files is a stronger result than the condition asked for and leaves no interpretive work behind. Criterion 11 remains satisfiedByEvidence on EVD-0008, which RUL-0006 recorded as the best evidence record the studio had produced and which I have not re-examined. Criteria 1-4 and 6-10 and 12 remain ADOPTED from RUL-0004 via RUL-0006 and are still not independently re-derived; nothing this round touched Assets/Core/Run/RunState.cs. Criterion 5 is the exception RUL-0006 ruled independently -- the relative reading governs -- and that ruling stands unaltered and is not revisited here. I also carry forward, unchanged, RUL-0004's and RUL-0006's record that criterion 5's delegation clause holds by INSPECTION ONLY, since no test can reach it through a sealed type's public API, and that the verifier's comment implying otherwise must not be read as evidence of it. Closure does not upgrade that grade.

nonBlockingLogged: MY OWN CONDITION NAMED AN AUTHOR THAT CANNOT WRITE. 'evaluatedBy: ci' was undischargeable by construction, because .github/workflows/gate-g2-code.yml uploads CI evidence as an artifact and deliberately never commits. Restated in matter 1 to what it was always for. The standing form, binding on me first: a condition on a record must be dischargeable by an actor capable of filing that record, and a director who names an owner field without asking whether that actor can hold a pen has written a condition that can only be met by falsifying it.

THE EVALUATOR AND THE ADJUDICATOR ARE THE SAME ACTOR AND NO CHECK NOTICES. IsNotSelfIssued separates the evaluator from the order's implementer, which is the invariant that matters most and which holds. It does not separate whoever ran the gate from whoever rules on closure, and in this round those are one. Sufficient here because the record names a re-runnable commit; weaker than an independent evaluator, and I decline to describe it as equivalent. Mine to build, and it pairs with the verdict-pointer defect recorded in RUL-0008 matter 3.

COMPLETION CANNOT NAME ITS VERDICT. task.schema.json's completedByGate is a gateId and the work order is additionalProperties: false, so no order file can say which verdict closed it. WO-0009 has one verdict so nothing turns on it here; WO-0008 has two and RUL-0008 matter 3 sets out why the shape is wrong before it bites. Recorded on both orders so the finding does not depend on someone reading the other ruling.

RegisterKill's throw still duplicates AddScore's message verbatim with nothing asserting they match, and AddScore validates before its IsOver check while RegisterKill checks IsOver first, with nothing in the XML doc explaining why two adjacent GameManager passthroughs behave oppositely on the same bad input. Carried forward unaltered from RUL-0004 and RUL-0006; neither cleared nor promoted. Closing this order does not resolve them and they remain quality's to detect, composing with the message-equality test already directed under WO-0010.

Criterion 12's engine-free clause still has no test, and RUL-0004's de-escalation stands: it is enforced mechanically by MergeSurvivor.Core.Build compiling Assets/Core against netstandard2.1 with no UnityEngine reference and warnings as errors. Not blocking, and I decline to re-sound an alarm a director has correctly quieted twice.

PRO-0003 remains status 'open' although WO-0009 was minted from it and is now delivered, adjudicated twice and closed. The triage backlog has been flagged by RUL-0002, RUL-0003, RUL-0004, RUL-0005 and RUL-0006 with nothing moving; RUL-0004 matter 5 records the concrete cost of a director at the five-proposal cap unable to file a finding it had already made. I set the priority in RUL-0005 and it has still not been taken, which is now a failure of execution rather than of prioritisation and is mine.

Studio/state/project-state.json still lists WO-0009 as 'queued' with no assignee, at version 5 and a day stale. Both orders are now completed and the file describes neither. Mine, deliberately not corrected in an adjudication pass, and overdue.

The order file stays in Studio/orders/open/ with status completed. The cross-check globs Studio/orders/**/WO-*.json so nothing breaks, but the directory name now contradicts the status on two orders. Cosmetic, and worth doing in the same pass as the project-state correction.

WO-0010 is untouched by this pass and remains open on RUL-0007's terms, including the blocking finding that its amended criterion 11 clause (2) states a monotonicity justification EVD-0006 has falsified. Nobody may read two closures as progress on that. It is a fresh technical adjudication reserved to me and it is the first thing after these two closures, exactly as RUL-0007 matter 4 said.

boundariesObserved: I wrote no production code and no test code and touched nothing under Assets/**. I amended no acceptance criterion; RUL-0006's reading of criterion 5 stands as a reading and I repeat that a reading is not an amendment and that if the absolute reading was intended the criterion is its author's to change and nobody else's. What I DID amend is a condition of my own prior ruling, which I restated in matter 1 rather than waived, with the defect and the reasoning set out at length so a reader can disagree with me; restating one's own condition is not the same as lowering a bar and I have tried to make the difference visible rather than assert it. I did not edit RUL-0006 to repair the defective condition in place -- the record is corrected by adding to it, which is the rule RUL-0007 matter 3 bound me to. I did not edit Studio/build, the kernel schemas, the constitution, CI, LESSONS.md, any proposal's status or any prior ruling. In Studio/orders/open/WO-0009.json I wrote exactly the three fields I was authorised to write and changed nothing else. I did not run the gate, override it or sign it; I ruled that a record of it having been run meets the standard, which is adjudication and not evaluation. I did not accept a manufactured record and I record in matter 2 that none was offered when one would have cleared a condition cheaply. I did not re-derive the eleven criteria adopted from RUL-0004 and said so. I did not escalate: the founder asked for closure and I am granting it on conditions I set publicly one pass earlier; nothing here touches the pillars, the non-goals, an irreversible action, monetisation or player data. I filed no proposal and no challenge.
whyNoChallenge: No criterion of WO-0009 is violated and none ever was. RUL-0004 checked all thirteen against the delivered RunState.cs and found the fix does exactly what the order asked; RUL-0006 disturbed none of that and resolved the one ambiguity by ruling rather than by converting it into a challenge. The two conditions left open this morning were a diff nobody had run and a record nobody could file, neither of which is a defect in the delivery. The one place a challenge might have been aimed -- an agent declining to satisfy a director's condition -- is the opposite of a fault: it refused to write 'ci' into a field where that would have been false, and brought the conflict back to the director who wrote the condition instead of engineering around it. Charging an agent for correctly refusing to falsify a record would be the single most damaging precedent available to me here. The defects this pass found are in my own conditions and in machinery RUL-0005 ruled is mine to design, and a director challenging itself is theatre where a ruling and a digest item are the honest instruments.
limitations: I have no shell, no git and no CI access. My instruments were reading the working tree, searching it, and reading .git/logs/HEAD -- which I had not thought to use in RUL-0006 and which replaces that ruling's weakest finding, the timestamp-based inference in its matter 3, with ancestry read from primary source. Five consequences. First and most important: I DID NOT RUN gate-g2.sh AND CANNOT CONFIRM ITS EXIT CODE AT de419a3. I read Studio/build/emit-gate-verdict.sh and satisfied myself that it cannot be told an answer, and I verified everything about the record that is verifiable from inside the repository, but 'G2 passed at de419a3' rests on that script having been run as the record says. What changed since RUL-0006 is not that I can confirm it; it is that the claim names a tree, so anyone with a shell can refute it. Second, the reflog tells me which commits exist and in what order and nothing whatever about their contents; if history were rewritten after those entries the ordering would be stale, though the entries I rely on are recent and consecutive. Third, I did not run the criterion 13 diff and could not; EVD-0012 carries that clause, and unlike WO-0008's diff I have no independent corroboration of it beyond the plausibility of its account of the window, since an empty numstat leaves nothing in the file to read against. That is the weakest evidential link in this closure and I would rather name it than let it sit inside a discharge. Fourth, my grading of criteria 1-4 and 6-10 and 12 is adopted from RUL-0004 through RUL-0006 and inherits whatever those readings were worth; both were produced without a shell. Fifth, my finding that no CI-authored record can exist in this repository rests on reading .github/workflows/gate-g2-code.yml as it stands today; it is the whole basis of matter 1, and if that workflow is later changed to commit from CI then the condition I restated should be revisited rather than treated as settled.
